articles.title: The Multi-Billion Dollar Tamiflu Con: How Roche Buried the Data and Governments Paid the Price
articles.summary: Tamiflu was stockpiled by governments worldwide at a cost of billions based on clinical trial data that was never fully published or independently verified. When the Cochrane Collaboration finally forced access to the complete trial data, the drug was shown to have minimal benefit over placebo. This is pharma fraud at a global scale — and regulators knew, or should have known.

articles.title: Niacin and Choline: The Buried Nutritional Science Behind the Fatty Liver Epidemic
articles.summary: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease is exploding in America, yet the upstream nutritional causes — including deficiencies in niacin and choline — are systematically ignored in favor of pharmaceutical interventions. Mercola's analysis points to dietary factors that the processed food and pharma industries have every incentive to keep out of clinical guidelines. The science exists; the will to act on it does not.

articles.title: Capricor Therapeutics Accused of Falsifying Clinical Trial Data — 64% Stock Collapse Exposes the Rot

This is the exact mechanism by which fraudulent trial data reaches patients: hype the data, get regulatory approval, cash out before the truth surfaces. Investors are collateral damage; patients are the real victims.

articles.title: Regeneron Under Fire: Class Action Alleges Investors Were Misled — What About Patients?

The question regulators refuse to ask: what did Regeneron know, when did they know it, and did any of it reach the FDA's desk?

articles.title: Hims & Hers Hit With FTC Lawsuit — Telehealth's Dirty Secret Is Finally Getting Scrutiny

The gap between what researchers know and what doctors prescribe is not accidental.

articles.title: CDC Quietly Merges Overdose Tracking Systems — Transparency Move or Data Control?
articles.summary: The CDC has consolidated three separate overdose surveillance systems into a single public dashboard, coinciding with a reported 12.3% drop in provisional overdose deaths to 67,798. While the decline is welcome, merging disparate datasets into one agency-controlled channel raises legitimate questions about data granularity, accountability, and whether inconvenient regional or demographic signals will survive the consolidation. Who controls the dashboard controls the narrative.

Gilead has built an HIV drug empire on reformulating existing compounds into new combinations that reset patent clocks and block generic competition — a strategy that costs patients and payers billions while offering marginal clinical advances. The FDA's approval pipeline functions as a pharma revenue protection service.
